rv.q: Izzard offering distinctive spins on every member of the court of Elsinore, popping in and out of them and breezily performing scenes opposite herself, much as she always has in her stand-up — and with results that are often as funny.
But Izzard's initial energy proves unsustainable over the course of five acts (adapter Mark Izzard cuts down Shakespeare’s text into two, but the meat of all five remains).
Izzard unfortunately fails to plumb the full pathos of the two key female figures.
This adaptation lacks an animating point of view beyond the stunt of having a single actor play all the roles.

cn.t: Izzard's solo Hamlet impresses as a feat of memorization across two dozen roles, but critics find it lacks the distinctive characterizations that made their Great Expectations triumph, working within a more limited dramatic palette.
